correctness.rationale: Exact intrinsic tangent gradient samples at four tetrahedral vertices yield an eight-by-eight Gram with entries d,x,z by differentiating the Legendre addition formula. The generic determinant factors exactly into powers 2,3,3 of three explicit linear factors, checked by symbolic expansion from the declared coordinates. Rational row reduction establishes all degree-zero through degree-twelve ranks; a separate harmonic-polynomial basis check reproduces degrees one through six and verifies the stated nullspace constraints. For every degree at least thirteen, Bernstein and Legendre recurrence/differential identities give strict bounds 6X+9/sqrt(l)<3 and 18X+9/sqrt(l)<9, ruling out every factor. All integer cutoffs and positive definiteness/normalization are addressed. The included checker executed successfully; no extrapolation is used.

value.rationale: Surjectivity of finite-node intrinsic gradient interpolation in a single spherical-harmonic eigenspace is an intrinsic sampling invariant. At the four regular tetrahedral nodes, degree four is onto (eight independent tangent coordinates), degree five unexpectedly loses three conditions (rank five), and every degree six and above recovers all measurements. Three explicit degree-five compatibility equations give directly usable obstructions. This nonmonotone exact-degree behavior is not implied by generic low-pass interpolation or general addition identities; the complete all-degree result is a motivated classification rather than arbitrary parameter slicing.
